info.title: Chord API
info.summary: Trade, data and agent endpoints for eight EVM chains (Ethereum 1, Arbitrum One 42161, Base 8453, BNB Chain 56, Avalanche 43114, Monad 143, Arc 5042, Robinhood Chain 4663) and Solana (data and swaps).
info.description:
Chord is a non-custodial trading app and on-chain data index. The API has three kinds of endpoint:

- **Trade**: `/quote` finds the best route across every venue on the chain; `/swap` turns it into a transaction you sign yourself. Chord never holds funds or keys.
- **Read**: every swap on the chain, rolled up by token, venue and hour, from Chord's own index — tokens, launches, holders, top wallets, portfolio PnL, liquidity positions and pools. No key needed. Avalanche, Base, BNB Chain, Arbitrum One and Ethereum have the same rollups under `/chains/{chain}/*`; Solana has its own data family under `/chains/solana/*` (base58 addresses, case-sensitive) and its swaps under `/sol/trade/*`.
- **Agent**: the analyst (`/ask`) and the streams.

Amounts are decimal strings in the token's smallest unit. Timestamps are Unix seconds unless the field is `updatedAt` (milliseconds). `GET /portfolio/{wallet}` and `/portfolio/{wallet}/activity` differ on both: amounts there are in whole tokens and every time is in milliseconds. Reads answer anonymous callers at 60 requests a minute per IP; an `X-API-Key` header raises that to your plan. Every non-2xx body is `{ error, message }`.

get.description:
Quotes every venue on the chain in parallel, splits the order across venues when that improves the output, composes a two-hop route through the chain's anchors when no direct pool wins, and returns the best.

**Use it for**: a price before a trade, a route card, an agent deciding whether to buy, a bot comparing venues.

**Notes**
- Amounts are strings in the token's smallest unit. On Arc the USDC predeploy has 6 decimals, native USDC 18 — send the predeploy address `0x3600…0000` (the zero address is an alias for it on 5042).
- A quote is a live read of the venues and is good for about 30 seconds. Re-quote before you build if you waited longer.
- `fast=1` returns a single-hop answer in about 400 ms marked `preliminary`; run the full quote alongside and replace it.
- `only=` pins one venue and bypasses the routing safety gates — it needs an API key.
- An empty `routePlan` is a real answer (no route at this size); read `noRouteReason`.

post.description:
Turns a quote into a transaction against the Chord router. You sign it and broadcast it; Chord never sees a key and never holds funds.

**Notes**
- Send the `/quote` body back unmodified. `chain` must match the quote.
- For an ERC-20 input, approve the router (`transaction.to`) for at least `inputAmount` first — or run `/swap/simulate` and let it tell you.
- `slippageBps` is a consistency check only: the signed minimum output is the quote's `otherAmountThreshold`. A different value is refused with `SLIPPAGE_MISMATCH` — re-quote at the slippage you want.
- On Arc the native sentinel aliases to the USDC predeploy: a "native" input is pulled by `transferFrom`, a "native" output is delivered as the predeploy, and `value` is always 0.
- `batch: "7702"` is Monad-only (EIP-7702 one-signature approve+swap); it is ignored on every other chain.

get.summary: Quote on any chain: Chord first, a fallback only when it fails
get.description:
One call that ends in a route you can sign or an honest "no route anywhere". Without `taker` it is a price; with `taker` it also returns the unsigned transaction, the approval it needs and a simulation.

**Policy**
1. Chord's own router is always asked first, with its normal budget.
2. A fallback is asked only when Chord fails: the engine timed out, errored or is down; there is no route; Chord refuses the route itself (value guard, taxed token, stale bonding-curve route); the chain's router is not live; or the built transaction fails simulation. A better price elsewhere is not a reason. A user error (unknown token, bad amount) never falls back.
3. Fallbacks are tried in the chain's order (`GET /meta/providers`); the first answer that passes every check wins. Per provider 4 s, whole request 9 s, a circuit breaker per provider and chain.

**Safety, on every fallback answer**
- The transaction target and the approval spender must be on Chord's allowlist for that provider and chain, and deployed there.
- `minAmountOut` comes from your slippage; a provider minimum below it is refused.
- The value guard of `/quote` applies: an output worth 30 % less than the input at Chord's prices is refused. An unpriced token gets a security scan (`safety`); a honeypot is refused.
- With `taker`, the transaction is simulated as that wallet and must deliver at least `minAmountOut`. A fallback transaction that cannot be simulated is never returned.
- Without `taker`, a fallback price is shown only after the provider BUILT the route and it was simulated for a placeholder wallet (`PRICE_CHECKED`); a provider that prices a size but will not build it is skipped. The placeholder's transaction is never returned.
- An input the simulation cannot supply (a balance that is not a plain storage mapping, e.g. rebasing shares) while the taker does not hold it: HTTP 422 `INPUT_NOT_SIMULATABLE` — hold the input and ask again.

**Notes**
- `provider: null` with HTTP 200 means every provider looked and none has a route. HTTP 503 `UNAVAILABLE` means nobody could answer right now: retry, do not conclude the pair is untradeable.
- The answer is good until `expiresAt` (30 s). Quote again before signing if you waited.

get.summary: Holdings and PnL on every chain
get.description:
What one wallet holds on Chord's eight EVM chains, and on Solana when you pass its Solana address, with its PnL over the last 24 hours, 7 days and 30 days. One rule for every chain, per token and window: the USD from its sales minus the USD of its buys inside the window, plus what is held now at today's price, minus what was held at the window's start at that hour's close. No cost basis is involved, and transfers are neutral: a token that arrived by transfer only adds its price move, and a quantity bought in the window that left with no sale on the tape (sent, bridged out) counts as sold at the window's average buy price, neither a gain nor a loss. Stablecoins are left out of PnL and counted in `cashUsd`.

**Use it for**: a wallet or portfolio page, "how did this wallet do this week", an agent sizing a trade against what the wallet already holds.

**Notes**
- **Coverage first.** A window is `complete` only when the chain's swap tape covers all of it. When it does not (the tape starts later, a hole in the history), `usd`, `pct` and `fromTs` are null: show a dash, never a partial number as a whole one. A total window is complete only when every chain in the answer is, chains that could not be read included. BNB Chain does not record swaps under $100: its windows still count as complete, and `coverage.ingestFloorUsd` says so.
- **Holdings** = the chain's token list plus every token the wallet swapped in the last 30 days, read on-chain (Solana: its 50 largest holdings). A token with no price Chord trusts (no measured liquidity, not on the chain's board) has `priceUsd: null`, comes last and is in no total. Priced holdings under $0.01 are folded into `dust`.
- **Each chain answers on its own deadline.** One that cannot be read is `status: "unavailable"` with a `reason` inside the 200 and is left out of the totals' value; `partial` = the balances were read, part of the rest was not.
- **Times are milliseconds** in this answer (`asOf`, `fromTs`, `tapeFromTs`), unlike most of this API.
- **Cache**: kept 45 seconds per wallet, Solana address and chain set (10 seconds when a chain could not be read); a copy up to 10 minutes old may be served once while a refresh runs (`asOf` says when it was computed). `fresh=1` recomputes, only for a request with an `X-API-Key` or an Ask session; otherwise it is ignored.
- **Without an API key (or an Ask session)**: a cached answer is served to anyone. One IP may start at most 10 new reads every 10 minutes (this route and `/activity` together), and every such caller together a limited number a minute; past either the answer is 429 `RATE_LIMITED` or 503 `BUSY` with `Retry-After`, and nothing is read. Send an `X-API-Key` for more.

Chord's analyst over the Arc index and the router — 40+ tools (trending, a token's flow, holders and risk, support and resistance, top traders on a token, a wallet's PnL and trades, largest prints, launches, depth, a bridge quote, read-only SQL over the index). Returns the answer, source links, an optional route card, tables and charts the analysis produced, and a report when one was built. It analyses: a plan (zones, tranches, an exit, the level where the idea is wrong) is written only when the question asks for one, and is illustrative, with its assumptions stated.

**Layout**: `text` is the whole answer on its own. The optional fields `shape`, `parts`, `details`, `followUpKinds` and `focus` say how the chat lays it out: `parts` is the same answer in order, with the tables and charts of `viz` placed inside the text (in `text` a placed table is written out as a Markdown table), and `details` is further depth the chat folds, which `text` does not repeat. A client that ignores them loses nothing of the answer.

**Auth**: a developer API key (`X-API-Key`) or a Google session bearer. Metered per key per day against the deployment's token budget; 8 questions a minute per caller.

**Agents**: send `"stream": false` for one JSON answer (5–40 s). Without it the response is `text/event-stream` with `status` events (which tool is running), `step` events (a lookup finished, with the chain it read), one `answer` event, then `done`.

get.description:
Chord's safety report for one token: the same report the Ask analyst, the trade dock and the trade card read.

**What runs**: on the EVM chains, Chord's own contract scan (proxy wiring and who can upgrade it, the owner and what the owner can do: mint, block wallets, pause, change taxes or limits), a $20 buy and its sell back through Chord's router simulated as a test wallet (nothing is sent), the transfer-tax probe, GoPlus, Sourcify and Chord's own tape screen (wash trading, buyer clusters, rugs, buyers who cannot sell, a copied ticker). On Solana: RugCheck, GoPlus, Jupiter and the screen of Chord's Solana tape (mint and freeze authority, Token-2022 extensions, LP lock, holders, the creator's history). A source that does not answer leaves its checks `unknown` and the report `partial`; it is never read as a pass.

**Use it for**: "is this token safe to buy", a rug or honeypot check before a trade, an agent's pre-trade gate (refuse `avoid`, warn on `caution`).

**Notes**
- Cached 10 minutes (2 to 3 minutes when a source did not answer, seconds when nothing could test selling an unvetted token or the check was cut short on Chord's side; such a partial report is sent `Cache-Control: private, max-age=10`). A report built cold on an EVM chain can take up to about 20 seconds. An address with no contract answers 404 at once.
- A report already cached answers anyone. Without an API key (or an Ask session), one IP builds at most 10 new reports every 10 minutes, and every such caller together a limited number a minute; past either the answer is 429 or 503 `BUSY` with `Retry-After`, and nothing is checked. Send an `X-API-Key` for more.
- `verdict` is decided in code from `checks`. No verdict rests on GoPlus alone: when only GoPlus answered, the report is `partial` and says Chord's own checks did not run. A reading from GoPlus names it "GoPlus (Powered by Go+ Security)".
- A Solana mint is used exactly as given (base58 is case-sensitive).

SOL/USDC and other major pairs therefore show far less volume than the whole market; the numbers are accurate for pump.fun, Meteora and Raydium style tokens. Transfers are not seen either: wallet PnL is average cost inside the window.

`pending` until the transaction is in a block, then `confirmed` / `finalized` with `receivedOut`, or `failed` / `expired` (its blockhash ran out; an RFQ order unseen for two minutes). Only transactions sent through `/sol/trade/send`.

**Open to everyone** since 2026-10-15, no key needed (an `X-API-Key` raises the rate limit). `/sol/trade/config` says whether the lane is on for the caller; when it is off the other routes answer `503 TRADE_NOT_ENABLED`.

A quote is SOL against one token, bought or sold. For every quote Chord builds, for **your wallet**, the transaction of each route — `direct` (Chord's own router: Raydium AMM v4 / CPMM / CLMM, Orca Whirlpool, Meteora DLMM / DAMM v2, Meteora DBC, Raydium LaunchLab, pump.fun, PumpSwap; up to two pools), `jupiter` (Jupiter's swap API, no Jupiter fee) and `jupiter_meta` (Jupiter's order: Metis, its RFQ market makers, DFlow, OKX; Jupiter's fee inside the amount) — simulates each on the chain and returns the one that leaves the wallet with the most: tokens for a buy, SOL for a sell, after every fee. Ties go to `direct`, then `jupiter`. A route handing back under half of the input's market value is refused.

Amounts are base units as decimal strings: lamports for SOL, the token's smallest unit otherwise. Addresses are base58, case-sensitive. Chord takes no fee on Solana today. Nothing is signed by Chord: you sign `quote.tx` unchanged and send it back.

get.description:
One bar-close strategy replayed over stored candles of a Hyperliquid perp or an FX pair / metal. Simulated: nothing is traded.

**Model** (the same text comes back in `assumptions`):
- A signal is computed on a CLOSED bar and filled at the NEXT bar's open.
- One position at a time, all-in (equity × `leverage`), long, short or both.
- `feeBps` is charged per side on notional. Default 4.5 for Hyperliquid, 1 for FX.
- `stopPct` / `takePct` are checked inside each bar against its high and low. When both could hit in the same bar the stop is taken first; a bar that opens beyond the level fills at its open.
- A position still open at the last bar is closed at that bar's close (`reason: "end"`). Equity at or below zero ends the run.
- No funding, no spread beyond the fee, no slippage. FX uses Dukascopy BID prices.

**Strategies and their parameters** (pass only the ones you want to change):

| `strategy` | Rule | Parameters (default) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `supertrend` | Long while the Supertrend direction is up, short while it is down. | `atr` (10), `mult` (3) |
| `ema_cross` | Long while EMA(`fast`) is above EMA(`slow`), short while below. | `fast` (20), `slow` (50) |
| `rsi` | Long when RSI falls below `lower`, short when it rises above `upper`, flat again when RSI crosses back through 50. | `length` (14), `lower` (30), `upper` (70) |
| `donchian` | Long on a close above the highest high of the previous `length` bars, short on a close below their lowest low; held until the opposite breakout. | `length` (20) |
| `buy_hold` | Always long. | none |

**Symbols**: any Hyperliquid perp by its coin id, matched without case (`BTC`, `eth`, `kPEPE`); a leading `$` and a trailing `USDT` / `USD` / `-PERP` are dropped. FX and metals: `EURUSD`, `GBPUSD`, `USDJPY`, `USDCHF`, `AUDUSD`, `USDCAD`, `USDSEK`, `NZDUSD`, `EURJPY`, `GBPJPY`, `EURGBP`, `XAUUSD` (also `gold`), `XAGUSD` (also `silver`).

**How much history there is**: the window is the last `days` ending now, cut to what the store holds. Hyperliquid candles start from what its API served when the store was built (1m a few days, 15m about seven weeks, 1h about seven months, 4h and 1d years) and grow from there; FX has 1h bars since 2016 and 1m bars for about the last 400 days (`/fx/lake` shows how far each symbol is filled). Fewer than 50 bars in the window is a `400` whose message says what the store keeps. Read `from`, `to` and `bars` in the answer for the window that was really tested.

function.name: chord_chains
function.description: The chains Chord serves, with their native asset, anchors and which capabilities each one has (overview, tokens, trades, candles, wallet PnL, smart money, holders, LP, quote, swap). Call this first when unsure what a chain supports.

function.name: chord_status
function.description: Live health of every chain: routing engine state, how old the newest indexed trade is, and the public status page link.

get.description: Engine, cache and pool-sync state. `503` when the routing engine is unreachable.

503.description: The lane behind this endpoint is not ready or not enabled here (`NOT_READY`, `CHAIN_NOT_ENABLED`, `NOT_ENABLED`, `*_UNAVAILABLE`). Retry later; do not treat it as an empty answer.

ApiKey.name: X-API-Key
ApiKey.description: Optional on every read. A key from getchord.xyz/developer raises the rate limit to your plan and meters usage per key. Required for `?only=` on quotes and for the Ask agent API.

Session.description: A Google sign-in session minted by the app (`nts_…`). Only the browser surfaces use it; agents use `ApiKey`.

AgentCounts.description: Counts for one surface or a sum of surfaces.

example.message: amount must be an integer string in the token's smallest unit

label.description: Short English label (`Sell tax`, `Owner can mint`).

status.description: `unknown` = the source that reads it did not answer, or nothing could test it. Never `pass` for a check that did not run.

detail.description: One sentence with the measured number (`Selling loses 40% to the token's own tax (Chord simulation 40%, GoPlus 40%).`).

source.description: Who read it, in words, at most 60 characters (`Chord simulation`, `Chord contract scan`, `Chord tape`, `RugCheck`, `Sourcify`). A reading from GoPlus says `GoPlus (Powered by Go+ Security)`.

address.description: The token (0x, lower-cased) or the Solana mint (case kept).

symbol.description: As the contract or the token list names it: chosen by whoever launched the token.

verdict.description: Decided in code from the checks, never by a model. `avoid`: it cannot be sold, a sell tax of 30% or more, a scam verdict of Chord's tape screen, or a copy of a listed token's ticker. `caution`: a check that warns (taxes of 5 to 30%, an owner who can mint, block wallets or pause, code one wallet can upgrade, unverified source, unlocked liquidity one provider can pull, top 10 holders over 60% …). `ok`: none of that, with two independent sources answering and a sell test passing. `unknown`: too few sources, or nothing could test selling it. Never read `ok` as a guarantee.

score.description: 0 (worst) to 100, in the verdict's band; null when the verdict is `unknown`.

checks.description: Every check, in a fixed order.

facts.description: The numbers behind the checks: `buyTaxPct`, `sellTaxPct`, `transferTaxPct`, `honeypot`, `owner`, `ownerRenounced`, `proxy`, `implementation`, `upgrader`, `verifiedSource`, `mintable`, `blacklist`, `pausable`, `lpLockedPct`, `top10Pct`, `holders`, `creator`, `creatorPct`, `screenLevel`, `screenReasons`, `simulation` (Chord's $20 buy and sell back: status, taxes, round trip), `reasons` (the counted reasons, worst first), `answered` / `missing` (the sources), `goplusOnly` (only GoPlus answered: the report is partial). Solana adds `mintAuthority`, `freezeAuthority`, `token2022Extensions`, `permanentDelegate`, `liquidityUsd`, `pools`, `topHolders`, `jupiterVerified`, `rugcheckScore` …

sources.description: Where to read it yourself (explorer, GoPlus, RugCheck, Sourcify, Jupiter).

checkedAt.description: Unix time, milliseconds — when the server built this answer.

partial.description: True when at least one source did not answer, or when GoPlus was the only one that did.

vetted.description: On a list Chord trusts (stock / ETF / bridged list token, the bridge provider's list, Monad's verified list, a registry anchor; on Solana Jupiter-verified majors): the issuer's own powers (mint, freeze, pause, upgrades) are listed but do not raise the verdict. Taxes and the sell test still count.

TokenRiskReport.description: Chord's safety report for one token.

stale.description: True when the most recent rolled-up hour is older than the lane's freshness bar.

floorHour.description: Oldest hour the rollup has reached so far.

backfillComplete.description: True once the rollup reaches genesis — before that, long windows undercount.

Coverage.description: How fresh and how deep the rolled-up data is. Trust these flags, not the clock.

symbol.description: Symbol from the contract, or null while unresolved.

impostor.description: True when the symbol copies the chain's anchor (a token called USDC that is not the USDC predeploy). Flagged, never hidden.

TokenLite.description: A token as it appears inside a pool row.

logoURI.description: Logo through Chord's proxy (`/v1/logo/5042/{address}`, 128 px WebP).

logoUriRaw.description: The upstream logo URL the proxy fetched, when there is one.

tags.description: `stablecoin`, `fx`, `stock`, … — from the curated list; empty for unlisted tokens.

listed.description: On the curated Arc token list (metadata and logo vetted).

priceUsd.description: Last trade price on the token's dominant venue, USD.

volume24h.description: USD, every venue, no dust floor.

traders.description: Distinct attributed wallets over the board's day window. Routers, executors and bots are not wallets.

totalSupply.description: `totalSupply()` in whole tokens. Null when unreadable.

marketCapUsd.description: totalSupply × price — fully diluted, since nothing on-chain says what is locked.

routable.description: The engine can quote this token today (at least one pool against a routing anchor).

flags.description: Honesty flags. `wash` = a day's volume carried by one or two wallets; `impostor` = an unlisted token wearing a listed symbol. Absent when clean.

ArcTokenRow.description: One token on Arc with its 24-hour tape.

launcher.description: Contract the creating transaction called (`create` = a raw deploy).

launcherName.description: Name from the launcher registry, when known.

tags.description: `stock`, `bridged`, `stablecoin`, …

RhTokenRow.description: One token on Robinhood Chain with its 24-hour tape.

navUsd.description: The issuer's published exchange rate at last refresh; null when none is published.

offHours7d.description: Activity outside the NYSE regular session (09:30–16:00 New York, weekdays) over the last seven days.

percent.description: Share of the input this leg carries.

pool.description: Pool address, or the 32-byte pool id on Uniswap V4.

inputAmount.description: Amount in the token's smallest unit, as a decimal string. Never a float.

outputAmount.description: Amount in the token's smallest unit, as a decimal string. Never a float.

adapter.description: The router adapter that executes this leg — from the engine, never hardcode.

feeAmount.description: Amount in the token's smallest unit, as a decimal string. Never a float.

inputAmount.description: Amount in the token's smallest unit, as a decimal string. Never a float.

outputAmount.description: Amount in the token's smallest unit, as a decimal string. Never a float.

otherAmountThreshold.description: Minimum output after fee and slippage — the number the transaction enforces.

priceImpactPct.description: Percent, as a string, against the spot rate of the same route.

routePlan.description: Empty with `outputAmount` "0" = no route (an honest answer, never a fabricated price).

noRouteReason.description: Only when `routePlan` is empty: `INSUFFICIENT_LIQUIDITY` (try a smaller amount) or `NO_POOLS`.

gasEstimate.description: Gas units, from the venue quoter or the RPC.

feeBps.description: Protocol fee on the output token, per token on-chain (`FeeCollector.feeBpsFor`): 5 bps by default on every chain, 0 on the stablecoins and majors a chain exempts (USDC / EURC on Arc, WETH / USDG and stocks on Robinhood Chain), capped at 100.

feeAmount.description: Amount in the token's smallest unit, as a decimal string. Never a float.

preliminary.description: Present only on `fast=1` answers: single-hop, ~400 ms, replace it with the full quote.

value.description: Amount in the token's smallest unit, as a decimal string. Never a float.

status.description: `ok`, or why this provider did not produce the answer: `no_route`, `timeout`, `http_error`, `rate_limited`, `invalid_response`, `not_allowlisted`, `calldata_mismatch`, `min_out_too_low`, `value_gap`, `unsafe_token`, `simulation_failed`, `unverified`, `breaker_open`, `skipped`; for Chord also `engine_error`, `engine_timeout`, `engine_down`, `route_refused`, `build_failed`, `chain_not_live`.

error.description: Short reason from a fixed vocabulary, never provider text.

MetaAttempt.description: One provider that was asked, in order.

amountIn.description: Amount in the token's smallest unit, as a decimal string. Never a float.

taker.description: The wallet the transaction was built and simulated for; null on a price-only quote.

provider.description: Who answered: `chord` (Chord's own router), `kyberswap`, `monorail`, `lifi`, `relay`. `null` = no provider has a route.

fallbackReason.description: `null` when Chord answered. Otherwise why it did not: `no_route`, `insufficient_liquidity`, `engine_error`, `engine_timeout`, `engine_down`, `value_guard`, `taxed_token`, `route_stale`, `chain_not_live`, `build_failed`, `simulation_failed`.

amountOut.description: What the taker receives after every fee, smallest unit of `tokenOut`. (`/quote`'s `outputAmount` is before Chord's fee; this is after.)

minAmountOut.description: The minimum the transaction enforces, from the slippage you asked for.

priceImpactPct.description: Percent, when the provider states one.

valueLossPct.description: Output value against input value at Chord's own prices, percent (negative = worth more). `null` when Chord has no reliable price for a side: see `safety` and `warnings`.

feeBps.description: Chord path: Chord's protocol fee on the output. Fallback: the integrator fee Chord added (0 today); the provider's own fees are already inside `amountOut`.

value.description: Amount in the token's smallest unit, as a decimal string. Never a float.

tx.description: The UNSIGNED transaction. `null` without `taker`. `to` is the Chord router when `provider` is `chord`, the provider's own router otherwise.

amount.description: Amount in the token's smallest unit, as a decimal string. Never a float.

resetFirst.description: Present only for a token that reverts `approve(x > 0)` while its allowance is non-zero (USDT on Ethereum). `true` = the taker has a left-over allowance: send `approve(spender, 0)` first, then this approval.

approval.description: The approval to send first. `null` for a native input or when the taker's allowance already covers the amount.

ok.description: `true` = ran and delivered at least `minAmountOut`; `null` = no verdict (only ever returned on the Chord path).

amountOut.description: Amount in the token's smallest unit, as a decimal string. Never a float.

simulation.description: The transaction run as the taker (with the input supplied when the taker does not hold it), measuring the taker's own balance change. `null` without `taker`.

safety.description: A security scan of the unknown token, present when the value check could not run on a fallback answer.

warnings.description: `INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE`, `UNPRICED`, `OUTPUT_WRAPPED`, `NO_ROUTE`, and on a price-only fallback `PRICE_CHECKED` (built and simulated for a placeholder wallet) or `UNVERIFIED_PRICE` (built, not simulatable) — each followed by a sentence.

MetaQuote.description: The same shape whichever provider answered.

pnlUsd.description: Realized plus open PnL at current prices.

smartScore.description: The ranking key: realized-weighted, luck-corrected, recency-decayed profit.

untrackedAmount.description: Balance that arrived by transfer (no cost basis).

usd.description: PnL over the window, USD. Null when the window is not complete.

pct.description: Percent (1.5 = +1.5 %) of the base: the value held at the window's start plus the USD bought in it. Null when that base is under one cent, or when the window is not complete.

complete.description: The swap tape covers the whole window with no known hole. False = `usd`, `pct` and `fromTs` are null: show a dash, never a number.

fromTs.description: Unix time, milliseconds. Where the number starts: the window's start, aligned down to the hour. On `totals`: the latest start of the chains.

PortfolioWindow.description: PnL over one window by the window rule (see `GET /portfolio/{wallet}`).

address.description: EVM token, lower-case. Null for the chain's native coin and on a Solana row (which carries `mint`).

mint.description: Solana rows only: the mint, case kept.

decimals.description: From the chain's list or the chain itself, never assumed.

native.description: The chain's own coin (ETH, MON, AVAX, BNB, USDC on Arc, SOL).

stable.description: A dollar stablecoin: counted in `cashUsd`, left out of PnL.

amount.description: Balance in whole tokens, as a decimal string.

priceUsd.description: Null = no price Chord trusts (no measured liquidity, not on the chain's board): listed last, in no total.

pnl.description: This token's part of each window's PnL, USD. Null = left out (a stablecoin, no price, no start price) or the chain's window is not complete.

PortfolioHolding.description: One token a wallet holds on one chain.

status.description: `ok` = read. `partial` = balances read, part of the rest (prices, the tape, some tokens) not, and `reason` says which. `unavailable` = not read at all: in no total, every window without a number.

reason.description: Present unless `ok`. One plain sentence for a person.

valueUsd.description: Sum of the priced holdings, small balances included.

cashUsd.description: The part of `valueUsd` held in stablecoins.

tapeFromTs.description: Unix time, milliseconds. First moment the chain's swap tape covers without a hole for this wallet. Null = no tape here.

source.description: `tape` = Chord's raw tape of the chain; `tape+lake` = older days joined from Chord's history lake; `box` = Chord's Solana index.

ingestFloorUsd.description: Present on a chain whose tape does not record swaps under this many USD (BNB Chain: 100). Disclosed, not a hole: that chain's windows still count as complete, and a swap under the floor reads only as a price move or a transfer. Say so next to the numbers.

holdings.description: Priced holdings worth at least $0.01, largest first, then the unpriced ones.

dust.description: Priced holdings under $0.01, counted here and not listed.

unpriced.description: Holdings with `priceUsd: null` (listed at the end of `holdings`).

sol.description: The Solana address as given, or null.

asOf.description: Unix time, milliseconds. When this answer was computed. A cached answer keeps its own `asOf`.

valueUsd.description: Sum of `valueUsd` over the chains that were read.

pnl.description: Complete only when every chain in the answer is complete for that window, chains that could not be read included. `pct` is the sum of the chains' USD over the sum of their bases.

Portfolio.description: One wallet on every chain in scope.

side.description: `buy` = the wallet received `token`; `sell` = it gave it.

address.description: EVM token, lower-case. Null on a Solana row.

tx.description: Transaction hash, or the Solana signature (case kept).

explorer.description: The transaction on the chain's explorer.

pool.description: A pool: a 20-byte contract address (V2 / V3) or a 32-byte Uniswap V4 pool id.

usd.description: Dollars that entered or left the pool.

priced.description: False when the event could not be valued (no anchor side).

tokenId.description: Position NFT id, for managed positions.

pool.description: A pool: a 20-byte contract address (V2 / V3) or a 32-byte Uniswap V4 pool id.

lpAccess.description: `hooked` = a V4 hook can refuse adds.

tokenSide.description: Which side is the non-anchor token (0 or 1).

aprPct.description: 24h fee/TVL × 365 — a full-range yardstick, not a promise.

suspect.description: Wash or launch-farm printing (volume without traders, dust TVL under real volume, turnover no honest pool reaches). Hidden by default; `flagged=1` shows them.

score.description: 0–100 health score (traders, TVL, yield sanity, LP flow, age, penalties).

marketCapUsd.description: The tracked token's price × its total supply on this chain (for a bridged token: what was bridged here). On the list only; `null` when the pool tracks neither side, the tracked side is the native coin, or the supply is not on record yet.

pool.description: A pool: a 20-byte contract address (V2 / V3) or a 32-byte Uniswap V4 pool id.

valueUsd.description: Live value of the liquidity (open positions).

edgePct.description: Distance from the price to the nearest range edge, percent.

jit.description: Opened and closed within seconds — a swap trick, shown but not scored.

unreconciled.description: Dollars out exceed dollars in by far — the tape missed an add; shown, never scored.

windows.description: Per window: the positions that ended or were last touched in it, the profit they made and the fees they collected over their life.

tokens.description: What the wallet provides to, by dollars in.

pool.description: A pool: a 20-byte contract address (V2 / V3) or a 32-byte Uniswap V4 pool id.

exits.description: Times the price left the range.

unreliable.description: Why the number should not be trusted, when it should not.

shareModel.description: What that share was measured against: the pool's in-range liquidity at its price now (V3 / V4 / Raydium CLMM), its active bin (Meteora DLMM), or its TVL counted as if spread over every price when the pool's depth could not be read (narrow ranges then read high).

SimResult.description: One range, backtested on Chord's own candles and the pool's real fee tier.

shapes.description: The pool templates this launcher creates.

minTradeUsd.description: Trades under this USD value (at index time) are not in the index, so every count, volume and candle covers trades at or above it. 0 = every priced trade.

history.description: Floors in force over time, oldest first. Empty when the chain was never floored. Raising a floor does not remove older, smaller rows.

IngestFloor.description: The tape's ingest floor. BNB Chain runs at $100 today; Avalanche and Base at 0.

stale.description: True when the last rollup pass is more than 30 minutes old.

symbol.description: Read from the contract. Null while unresolved.

logoURI.description: Always null on these chains for now.

priceUsd.description: Last print on the token's busiest venue, USD.

volume24h.description: USD, every venue, trades at or above the ingest floor.

dominantDex.description: Venue id with the most 24-hour volume.

ChainTokenRow.description: One token on a chain-keyed chain with its 24-hour tape. No curated list, no honesty flags, no trader counts yet.

ChainVenueShare.description: One venue's share of the window.

token.description: Solana address, base58, case-sensitive. Never lower-case it.

symbol.description: Creator-chosen; null until the metadata worker has read it.

image.description: Image URL from the token's metadata, as published by its creator.

priceUsd.description: Last price on the token's main pool (traded in the last hour first, then the deepest).

change24hPct.description: Price now against the main pool's close 24 hours ago.

volume24hUsd.description: USD over the 24-hour window, every pool the tape reads.

liquidityUsd.description: Main pool: twice its quote-side reserve in USD, from the last swap whose event carried the reserve. An estimate; null when unknown.

pool.description: Solana address, base58, case-sensitive. Never lower-case it.

oneWayPct.description: Percent of the 24-hour dollar volume traded by wallets that went one way: each wallet's smaller side (bought or sold, in USD) under half its larger side. The rest is wallets buying and selling about the same amounts back and forth: arbitrage, market making or wash trading. Null when not measured.

screen.description: Why the boards leave this token out, or null. `volume bot`: under 10 % of its 24-hour volume came from one-way wallets and it is not a deep market (at least $250k of SOL / stable liquidity turned over at most 10× in the window). `impostor`: the ticker of SOL, USDC or USDT, look-alike letters included, on another mint.

SolTokenRow.description: One Solana token with its 24-hour tape.

token.description: Solana address, base58, case-sensitive. Never lower-case it.

priceUsd.description: Current price on the main pool.

heldAmount.description: Bought minus sold inside the window, whole tokens (never below 0). Not the on-chain balance.

realizedPnlUsd.description: Matched amount × (average sell − average buy). Null when the window has sells but no buys.

partial.description: Sold more than it bought inside the window: part of the position was bought before the window (or arrived by transfer), so those sells carry no cost basis.

SolPosition.description: One token in a wallet's window.

position.description: Solana address, base58, case-sensitive. Never lower-case it.

pool.description: Solana address, base58, case-sensitive. Never lower-case it.

owner.description: Solana address, base58, case-sensitive. Never lower-case it.

mintA.description: Solana address, base58, case-sensitive. Never lower-case it.

mintB.description: Solana address, base58, case-sensitive. Never lower-case it.

lower.description: DLMM bin id or CLMM tick.

realizedPnlUsd.description: Withdrawn + fees − deposited; null unless closed, not partial and fully priced.

partial.description: The tape did not see the open (opened before `since`); PumpSwap: more came out than the tape saw going in.

unpricedEvents.description: Value events without a USD price.

route.description: `direct` = Chord's own route (pump pools or Chord's router) · `jupiter` = Jupiter's swap API · `jupiter_meta` = Jupiter's order (RFQ makers, DFlow, OKX).

mint.description: Solana address, base58, case-sensitive. Never lower-case it.

inAmount.description: What the wallet puts in: lamports for a buy, the token's smallest unit for a sell.

networkFeeLamports.description: Base + priority fee the wallet pays; 0 when Jupiter or a market maker pays (`gasless`).

walletLamportsDelta.description: The wallet's whole SOL change in the simulation, network fee and rent of new accounts included.

lastValidBlockHeight.description: After this block height the transaction can no longer land.

venue.description: `direct` only: where it trades (the largest leg when the order is split): `pumpswap`, `pumpfun`, `raydium_v4`, `raydium_cpmm`, `raydium_clmm`, `orca`, `meteora_dlmm`, `meteora_damm_v2`, `meteora_dbc`, `raydium_launchlab`.

layout.description: `direct` on a pump pool: the instruction layout copied.

solBased.description: A PumpSwap pool whose base is SOL.

pool.description: Solana address, base58, case-sensitive. Never lower-case it.

partial.description: A pump.fun curve had fewer tokens left than the input buys: the quote takes all it has, for at most `inAmount`.

pool.description: Pool.

hops.description: The legs: Chord's router (one or two pools) or Jupiter's route plan.

gasless.description: `jupiter_meta`: Jupiter or the market maker pays the network fee; the wallet is a second signer.

expireAt.description: `jupiter_meta` RFQ quotes: Unix seconds the market maker's price lives to. Ask again when under ten seconds are left.

route.description: `direct` = Chord's own route (pump pools or Chord's router) · `jupiter` = Jupiter's swap API · `jupiter_meta` = Jupiter's order (RFQ makers, DFlow, OKX).

mint.description: Solana address, base58, case-sensitive. Never lower-case it.

wallet.description: Solana address, base58, case-sensitive. Never lower-case it.

sends.description: How many times Chord sent it (every 2 seconds until it lands or its blockhash expires).

quotedOut.description: Base units as a decimal string (lamports for SOL).

receivedOut.description: What the wallet really got, read from the landed transaction with the quote's measure.
